title: WiFi Transceiver
summary: A custom ESP32 circuit board built to explore high-frequency PCB design and antenna placement.

cover.alt: Assembled green WiFi Transceiver board with a central ESP32 chip and two push buttons

sections.heading: The brief
paragraphs: For the ENGR 342 capstone I designed a small WiFi board around an ESP32-C3 from scratch. The goal was to treat the radio as the hard part of the design: a board that connects and programs easily is only useful if the antenna, supply, and clock around the chip are laid out with care.

sections.heading: Schematic
paragraphs: The circuit is a USB-C port feeding a 3.3 V regulator, which powers the ESP32-C3 through a bank of decoupling capacitors. A crystal sets the clock and a chip antenna sits on the RF line through a small matching network. Enable and Boot buttons allow resetting and flashing the chip, a status LED shows power, and spare GPIO pins are broken out to headers.
Keeping the schematic divided by function (power, RF, clock, and I/O) made it easier to check each block before committing it to a layout.

images.alt: Schematic with USB-C input, voltage regulator, status LED, reset button, boot button, GPIO headers, crystal, antenna, and the ESP32-C3
images.caption: Schematic drawn in KiCad, grouped by power, RF, clock, and I/O.

sections.heading: Layout and antenna placement
paragraphs: High-frequency layout is mostly about what goes where. The decoupling capacitors and crystal are placed around the ESP32-C3, and the antenna is positioned with its matching components so the RF path stays short.
The board uses two copper layers. The silkscreen carries the course number, project name, and a Ø mark.

images.alt: Two-layer PCB layout in red and blue with the ESP32-C3 at the top centre, a USB-C connector at the bottom, and the project name in the silkscreen
images.caption: PCB layout: red is the top copper layer and blue is the bottom.

sections.heading: The finished board
paragraphs: The finished board was assembled with the ESP32-C3 at its centre and the Enable and Boot buttons within easy reach for flashing over USB-C.
